[#hash-password-hashing-compare]
.What each of "Password hashing" is
[cols="2,1,3,2,1,2",options="header"]
|===
| Name | Output | Security | Standard | Status | In the browser (WebCrypto)

| <<hash-argon2id,`argon2id`>>
| 16 to 2^32 - 1 bytes
| each guess costs its memory and passes, on a GPU too
| RFC 9106, one lane
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-scrypt,`scrypt`>>
| 1 to (2^32 - 1) times 32 bytes
| each guess costs 128 r N bytes of memory
| RFC 7914
| recommended
| no
|===

[#hash-password-hashing-choose]
.How to choose among "Password hashing"
[cols="2,2,2,4,4",options="header"]
|===
| Name | Fastest natively | Smallest on Emscripten | Where it is used | Choose it when

| <<hash-argon2id,`argon2id`>>
| 37.8 ms (sodium)
| 39,690 bytes (sodium)
| link:https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html[OWASP's first choice for password storage]; link:https://www.password-hashing.net/[the Password Hashing Competition's winner]; link:https://bitwarden.com/help/kdf-algorithms/[Bitwarden's vault key, as an option]
| Storing passwords and deriving keys from them.

| <<hash-scrypt,`scrypt`>>
| 18.7 ms (sodium)
| 29,540 bytes (sodium)
| link:https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/data-structures-and-encoding/web3-secret-storage/[Ethereum's keystore files (Web3 Secret Storage)]; link:https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html[OWASP: N 2^17, r 8, p 1 when Argon2id is not available]
| When a format demands scrypt; otherwise Argon2id.
|===

The measured columns are doc/measurements.json's (2026-11-16, Apple M5 Max): the native throughput over 1 MiB, or the time of one derivation over `hmac_sha2_256`, of the fastest backend, and the smallest Emscripten program that calls the function; <<hash-measurements>> has every backend on every target. The data was measured on a loaded, shared machine, so close figures may swap at the next measurement.
